name: Frank Slootman
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Snowflake Inc.; independent director, Nscale (AI data-centre company, since Oct 2026)
profile: Dutch-born software executive who took three companies public: Data Domain (sold to EMC for $1.8B in 2009), ServiceNow (2012 IPO) and Snowflake (record 2020 IPO). Stepped down as Snowflake CEO in Feb 2024 but remains chairman; in Oct 2026 joined the board of UK AI-infrastructure firm Nscale. Author of 'Amp It Up' (2022).
interesting_fact: Before taking the Snowflake CEO job in 2019 he was retired and racing sailboats competitively in the San Francisco Bay Area; in Oct 2026 he joined the board of AI data-centre builder Nscale, highly relevant to a data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a military veteran and a portrait artist, he raced sailing dinghies as a boy, was a standout economics student at Erasmus University Rotterdam, and finished early to chase US internships - his dream employer was IBM. 'Amp It Up' began as a 2018 LinkedIn article.
notes: Snowflake press contact is a corporate route; Nscale board role is the natural hook for an energy/data-center podcast. Has appeared on podcasts promoting 'Amp It Up' so is media-accessible.

name: Xiao Yongming
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Zangge Mining (000408.SZ); control transferred to Zijin Mining in 2025
profile: Sichuan-born entrepreneur who ran a plastics factory in Anyue County before moving to Golmud, Qinghai, and founding Golmud Zangge Potash in 2002. Zangge Mining (potassium chloride, lithium carbonate, stake in Tibet Julong Copper) listed via backdoor in 2016. In 2025 the family agreed to sell control (25%) to Zijin Mining; his sons Xiao Yao and Xiao Ning have led the company.
interesting_fact: He moved to Golmud in 1996 to work in catering, then jumped into potash in 2002; by 2016 Hurun ranked him the richest person in Qinghai with 26.5 billion yuan.
deep_cut_fact: In 1981, aged about 17, he started at the Yonghong Plastics Factory in Anyue County, Sichuan, rising to factory director; the family's Sichuan Yonghong Industrial still carries that name.
notes: Sensitive: detained in 2021 (illegal-mining probe) and under residential surveillance Apr-Oct 2024 (lifted); avoid in outreach. Control of Zangge sold to Zijin (deal signed Jan 2025, https://www.jiemian.com/article/12253064.html). No personal media presence; any route would be via Zangge board secretary office.

name: Jacques Bouriez
current_role: Chairman (président), Louis Delhaize Group (Charleroi, Belgium); operations run by sons François and Pierre Bouriez
profile: Member of the Bouriez family that controls Belgian-French retailer Louis Delhaize Group (Cora hypermarkets, Match, Smatch, Delitraiteur). Brother of Cora founder Philippe Bouriez (d. 2014). Moved from CEO to chairman when his sons became joint managing directors. The group has since been unwinding: Cora France sold to Carrefour (2024), Belgian Cora stores closed by early 2026.
interesting_fact: Louis Delhaize Group traces its roots to 1875 in Charleroi; Jacques's brother Philippe Bouriez founded the Cora hypermarket chain, and the family held the group for decades as one of Europe's last big private grocers.
notes: Very private, elderly; no death reported in searches (only brother Philippe's, 2014: https://www.lsa-conso.fr/philippe-bouriez-mort-d-un-grand-nom-de-la-distribution-francaise,166753). Group is being dismantled (https://www.retaildetail.eu/news/food/dismantling-of-ldz-louis-delhaize-group-nears-completion/), so poor fit for podcast; any route would be via Louis Delhaize SA corporate office. Shares listing with Philippe Bouriez (deceased).

name: Norbert Dentressangle
current_role: Founder; chairman/president of family holding Dentressangle (formerly Dentressangle Initiatives), Lyon - day-to-day co-chaired by his children
profile: Born 1954 in Annonay, he joined his parents' Rhone-valley trucking firm in 1974 and founded Norbert Dentressangle SA in 1979, building it into a European logistics leader (43,000 staff, $5.5B revenue) before selling to XPO Logistics for $3.53B in 2015. He now invests via the family holding in real estate and industry (e.g. Kiloutou), with a plan to deploy EUR 1B.
interesting_fact: He wrote 'Passion Rouge', a book about his entrepreneurial journey - the red refers to the group's iconic red trucks, long a familiar sight on European motorways.
deep_cut_fact: His breakthrough niche was the Saint-Vallier (Drome) to London run: in 1979 he set up a new company focused on that route, starting with about 40 tractors - which is why his red trucks became so familiar to British drivers.
notes: Low-profile; holding now led day-to-day by children Pierre-Henri and Marine Dentressangle (co-chairs). Born 9 July 1954 in Annonay (https://www.lyonmag.com/profil-personnalite-lyonnaise/301/norbert-dentressangle/25). Best route: holding's contact form.

name: Eduard Schleicher
current_role: Managing partner / co-managing director, SCHWENK Zement GmbH & Co. KG (Ulm); supervisory board member at PAUL HARTMANN AG and Wieland-Werke AG
profile: Fifth-generation member of the Schwenk family behind Ulm-based SCHWENK, a cement maker founded in 1847 that now also spans concrete, sand & gravel and concrete pumps, with ~4,500 staff across Germany and Central/Eastern Europe. Schleicher co-leads the group and drives its international expansion; he formerly sat on Heidelberg Materials' supervisory board.
interesting_fact: SCHWENK's Mergelstetten cement plant hosts catch4climate, a >EUR120M oxyfuel carbon-capture pilot run jointly with rivals Heidelberg Materials, Buzzi/Dyckerhoff and Vicat; it captured its first high-purity CO2 (as dry ice) in July 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal coverage. catch4climate CO2 capture is a strong energy/decarbonisation angle; route via SCHWENK corporate communications. Board roles per https://de.marketscreener.com/insider/EDUARD-SCHLEICHER-A09UUA/ (aggregator).

name: Gerald J. Ford
current_role: Chairman, Hilltop Holdings (NYSE: HTH); co-managing partner, Ford Financial Fund; director, Mechanics Bank
profile: Dallas lawyer-turned-banker (b. 1944, raised in Pampa, Texas; SMU grad) who has bought and turned around distressed banks since 1975. His biggest win was selling Golden State Bancorp (with Ronald Perelman) to Citigroup for ~$6B in 2002. He owns ~25% of Hilltop Holdings (PlainsCapital Bank, PrimeLending, HilltopSecurities) and controls California's Mechanics Bank via Ford Financial Fund.
interesting_fact: He gave his alma mater SMU $20M in 1997 for a new football stadium (Gerald J. Ford Stadium) and $15M in 2013 for a research center.
deep_cut_fact: Ford credits working as a teenager in an auto body shop alongside his dad in Pampa, Texas, with pushing him toward a better career - and he carried around Ayn Rand's 'Atlas Shrugged' in high school.

public_contacts.value: mdunn@hilltop.com (Matt Dunn, Hilltop Holdings investor relations)

notes: Not to be confused with the US president. Son Jeremy Ford is Hilltop CEO. Low media profile; IR contact is a corporate route, not personal.

name: Hanni Toosbuy Kasprzak
current_role: Chairman of the Board, ECCO Sko A/S and ECCO Holding (Bredebro, Denmark); board member, The Toosbuy Foundation
profile: Daughter of shoemaker Karl Toosbuy, who founded ECCO with Birte Toosbuy in Bredebro, Denmark, in 1963. She joined the company straight out of school, became board chair in June 1996 and took majority ownership in 1997. ECCO is one of the few big shoe brands that owns its value chain, from tanneries to stores; her son Andre Kasprzak sits on the board.
interesting_fact: ECCO is a vertically integrated shoemaker that owns its own tanneries and factories - unusual among global footwear brands - and has been controlled by one family from tiny Bredebro in southwest Denmark since 1963.
deep_cut_fact: Her first job after school was as an ECCO quality controller in India in 1978/79, before returning to headquarters in Bredebro to work across several departments.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed. Husband Dieter Kasprzak was long-time ECCO CEO. Avoid ECCO's Russia-operations controversy in outreach. Route via ECCO group press office.

name: Zhang Wanzheng (Zhang Wanzhen, 张万镇)
current_role: Founder and actual controller (~22% stake) of Chaozhou Three-Circle (Group) Co. (300408.SZ); chairman 1992-2021, succeeded by Li Gang
profile: Born 1949, he rose from factory worker to director of Chaozhou's state radio-porcelain factory, which he restructured in 1992 into Three-Circle (CCTC). The company became a leader in advanced electronic ceramics - optical-fibre ceramic ferrules, ceramic substrates, MLCCs and solid-oxide fuel-cell components. He handed the chairmanship to Li Gang in 2021 but remains the controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Holding up a fibre-optic ceramic ferrule in a 2026 interview, he noted its bore is accurate to 1/60 of a hair's width; 20 years of in-house R&D broke foreign makers' monopoly and cut the part's price from ~100 yuan each to under 0.4 yuan.
deep_cut_fact: He started work at 16 and spent eight years at the Chaozhou No.2 Light Industry Bamboo-ware Factory, then 19 years at the radio porcelain factory, working his way up to factory director before founding Three-Circle in 1992.
notes: Name usually romanised Zhang Wanzhen. Was once a Chaozhou vice-mayor. Very relevant to data-center/optical/fuel-cell themes, but rarely gives interviews; route via board secretary office (email from 2023 annual-report summary - verify latest report).

name: Zhou Zerong (Chau Chak Wing, 周泽荣)
profile: Guangdong-born Chinese-Australian businessman (Teochew/Chaozhou roots) who went to Hong Kong young, moved to Australia in the 1980s and founded Guangzhou's Kingold Group in the early 1990s, spanning property, education, agriculture, hospitality, healthcare, media and banking. A major Australian university donor and Australian citizen.
interesting_fact: He funded the Frank Gehry-designed 'paper bag' Dr Chau Chak Wing Building at UTS Business School in Sydney - Gehry's first building in Australia - and the Chau Chak Wing Museum at the University of Sydney (opened 2020).
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he founded the annual Imperial Springs International Forum in Guangdong (hosting e.g. the China-Australia Economic Forum); he is also a Fellow of the Australian War Memorial and Honorary Ambassador of veterans' charity Soldier On.
notes: Politically sensitive figure in Australia (past political donations, high-profile defamation litigation) - handle carefully and avoid those topics. No published direct contact found; Kingold site unreachable. Possible routes: Imperial Springs International Forum organisers or his university philanthropy offices.

name: Lachhman Das Mittal
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus-style patriarch, Sonalika Group (International Tractors Ltd), Hoshiarpur, Punjab; operations run by sons and grandsons
profile: Born 1931 in Punjab, a former LIC insurance officer who began making threshers in 1970 and scaled the business after retiring around age 60. Sonalika (International Tractors) is now India's third-largest tractor maker and a major exporter; Japan's Yanmar holds 30%. Often called India's oldest billionaire, he has handed operations to sons Amrit Sagar and Deepak Mittal and grandsons.
interesting_fact: Sonalika ('lines of gold' in Hindi) is named after a wheat seed variety that fuelled India's Green Revolution.
deep_cut_fact: In 1970, while still an LIC agent, he began building wheat threshers with the help of local blacksmiths in Hoshiarpur, Punjab - the seed of what became the Sonalika tractor empire.
notes: About 95 years old; no death reported in searches (Nov 2026). Spelled Lakshman Das Mittal on Wikipedia. Realistic podcast guests would be son Deepak Mittal or grandson Raman Mittal (exec directors). Route via Sonalika corporate.

name: Ben Pon Jr.
profile: Died 30 September 2019 in Nijkerk, aged 82. Son of Pon founder Ben Pon Sr.; led the family firm Pon Holdings (VW/Porsche importer) 1965-1988, was a Porsche racing driver (one F1 start, Zandvoort 1962), a 1972 Munich Olympic clay-pigeon shooter and later a winemaker.
interesting_fact: The main grandstand at Circuit Zandvoort was renamed the 'Ben Pon Tribune' in his honour.
notes: Deceased (source: https://www.gpblog.com/nl/nieuws/oud-formule-1-coureur-en-porsche-importeur-ben-pon-overleden.html ; https://autorai.nl/mister-porsche-is-niet-meer/). Pon Holdings is now owned/run by other family branches and professional management (Pon is a big e-bike/mobility group - Gazelle, Cervelo).

name: Hugo Mann
profile: Died 20 December 2008 in Baden-Baden, aged 95. German retail pioneer who opened a furniture shop in Karlsruhe in 1938, founded Wertkauf (Germany's first self-service hypermarket chain, 1958; sold to Walmart in 1997 after son Johannes took over) and the Mann Mobilia furniture chain (1970; sold to Lutz group 2005).
interesting_fact: In 1975 he bought two-thirds of US discount chain FedMart, founded by Sol Price, who went on to create Price Club - the forerunner of Costco.
notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Mann ; Lebensmittelzeitung obituary https://www.lebensmittelzeitung.net/handel/personalien/Hugo-Mann-70969). Listing is a 1996-2000 Forbes entry.

name: Christine Volkmann
current_role: Shareholder (Volkmann family branch), Brose Fahrzeugteile SE & Co. KG (Coburg/Bamberg auto-parts supplier)
profile: Sister of longtime Brose chief Michael Stoschek and co-owner of family-held Brose, the mechatronics auto supplier (doors, seats, motors, e-bike drives) founded by her grandfather's family firm in 1908. Brose is owned 100% by the Stoschek and Volkmann families; she is not involved in management and has almost no public profile.
interesting_fact: Brose is wholly owned by two family branches - Stoschek and Volkmann - and its governance gives the advisory board the deciding say if the two families deadlock.
notes: Name collision: NOT the Wuppertal entrepreneurship professor Christine Volkmann (b.1960). Identity as Brose shareholder/sister of Michael Stoschek per Tharawat; no personal details or confirmation of current status found. Older Brose releases (2021, presseportal.de) list presse@brose.com as group communications mailbox - verify. Poor podcast fit.

name: Lei Jian (雷健)
current_role: Director and Vice President, HKC Corporation (惠科股份, Shenzhen display-panel maker); member of board strategy committee
profile: Co-founding executive of HKC, the Shenzhen-based maker of LCD/Mini-LED display panels and smart-display terminals (revenue ~40B yuan in 2024) controlled by founder Wang Zhiyong. He joined as vice president when HKC was set up in December 2001 and, with Xu Qiang, holds Shenzhen Jinfeiyang, HKC's second-largest shareholder (~16%). His Hurun wealth reflects HKC's Shenzhen main-board IPO process.
interesting_fact: HKC is one of China's biggest panel makers, with large state-backed fabs in Mianyang, Chuzhou, Changsha and elsewhere; it showcased a 5K RGB Mini LED panel at ChinaJoy 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a teacher - first at the national meteorological administration's Nanchang Meteorological School, then at Buxin Middle School in Shenzhen's Luohu district - before joining HKC as vice president at its founding in December 2001.
notes: Very low profile; no personal media presence. Contact would be via HKC board secretary office (see HKC/001399 prospectus on cninfo: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-06-04/1225350393.PDF); HKC website not reachable from here.

name: Catherine Phillips
current_role: Co-founder and co-funder (with husband John Phillips), Northpine Foundation (Canada); retired psychologist
profile: Toronto-area psychologist (EdD, C.Psych) who specialised in helping cancer patients manage stress, leading relaxation/support groups at Wellspring and the Healing Journey program. She and husband John Phillips were early Shopify investors (~2% combined; John was on Shopify's board 2010-2023). Since 2021 their Northpine Foundation has committed about C$290M to 300+ ventures for under-served Canadians.
interesting_fact: In a May 2026 founders' letter, she and John wrote that after donating $130M to 100+ ventures they 'were not as good as we hoped at investing impactfully' and re-tooled Northpine to measure 'social ROI' - cost per person moved from precarity to stable, taxpaying life.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shopify wealth, she was a health contributor to Chatelaine magazine and wrote 'Calm Your Mind and Warm Your Heart' (2011; 2013 edition subtitled real voices and techniques for cancer), drawn from 15+ years leading the Healing Journey program for people with cancer.
notes: Goes by Cathy. Low public profile; best route is the Northpine contact form (media-request category). Staff emails on the About page are for grantees - not appropriate for this outreach. Shopify/early-investor story is the entrepreneurship hook.

name: Cheng Yong (程涌)
current_role: Chairman, Aoshikang Technology Co. (奥士康, 002913.SZ), printed-circuit-board maker; also chairman of Aoshikang Precision Circuit (Huizhou)
profile: Born 1974, he built Shenzhen Aoshikang Electronics into Aoshikang Technology, a PCB manufacturer with major plants in Yiyang (Hunan) and Huizhou supplying boards for servers, automotive and consumer electronics. He has been chairman since October 2015; the company listed in Shenzhen in 2017 and in October 2026 its board approved plans for a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 he chaired the board meeting approving Aoshikang's plan to issue H-shares and list in Hong Kong, adding a second listing to its Shenzhen A-shares.
deep_cut_fact: His official company biography lists only a high-school education - he built a multi-billion-yuan circuit-board maker without a university degree, rising from chairman/GM of Shenzhen Aoshikang Electronics to chairman of the listed group.
notes: Very low media profile. PCB for servers/AI hardware is a possible data-center angle. Route via securities department (board secretary Yin Yunyun per 2025 annual report).
